Projective spaces over \mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z The space \mathbb P^d(\mathbb Z / N\mathbb Z) is the set of vectors (x_0,\ldots,x_d) \in (\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z)^{d+1} such that \gcd(x_0,\ldots,x_d,N) = 1, modulo multiplication by units of \mathbb Z / N \mathbb Z.
The function FiniteProjectiveSpace takes the dimension d and the level N. It returns a record containing a list Reps with one representative of each point, and a function RepOf that returns the representative of a given vector. Note that the length of Reps equals, in both cases, the index of the corresponding subgroup built there. This is because SL_n(\mathbb Z)/\Gamma_0(N) \cong \mathbb P^{n-1}(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z).

Integral homology modulo the primes 2 and 3 The group SL_3(\mathbb Z) acts cellularly on a 3-dimensional contractible regular CW complex K, with finite cell stabilizers of order dividing 24. Hence the finite index subgroup \Gamma_0(N) also acts on K. The quotient Y=K/\Gamma_0(N) has the same integral homology as \Gamma_0(N) away from the primes 2 and 3: the free parts and the p-torsion for p \geq 5 agree, while the 2 and 3-torsion may differ. For N=31, the following example computes H_1(Y,\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z_{5}, H_2(Y,\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z_3 and H_3(Y,\mathbb Z)= \mathbb Z^4.

Low-dimensional integral homology To compute the homology exactly, including the 2- and 3-torsion, we need a free \mathbb Z\Gamma_0(N)-resolution. Its tensor product with \mathbb Z gives H_n(\Gamma_0(N),\mathbb Z), at a higher computational cost than the quotient Y. The following example computes H_1(\Gamma_0(31),\mathbb Z)= \mathbb Z_{30}, H_2(\Gamma_0(31),\mathbb Z)= (\mathbb Z_2)^8 , H_3(\Gamma_0(31),\mathbb Z)=(\mathbb Z_6)^2 \oplus (\mathbb Z_{12})^2 \oplus \mathbb Z^4.
